tasks.question: How old does Heathcliff say Isabella Linton is on the night he and Cathy watch the Lintons through the window at Thrushcross Grange?
tasks.required_document_text: Isabella—I believe she is eleven, a year younger than Cathy—lay screaming at the farther end of the room, shrieking as if witches were running red-hot needles into her.

tasks.question: How many days was old Mr. Earnshaw away on the journey from which he brought the child Heathcliff home?
tasks.required_document_text: It seemed a long while to us all—the three days of his absence—and often did little Cathy ask when he would be home.

tasks.question: How much more careless and uncared for does Nelly say Heathcliff had become since Catherine's stay at the Grange?
tasks.required_document_text: If he were careless, and uncared for, before Catherine’s absence, he had been ten times more so since.

tasks.question: Which two servants were the only ones who would stay at Wuthering Heights under Hindley's tyrannical conduct?
tasks.required_document_text: The servants could not bear his tyrannical and evil conduct long: Joseph and I were the only two that would stay.

tasks.question: How does Catherine mockingly tell Ellen to lay the tables when Heathcliff comes to tea at the Grange?
tasks.required_document_text: Set two tables here, Ellen: one for your master and Miss Isabella, being gentry; the other for Heathcliff and myself, being of the lower orders.

tasks.question: Whom does Heathcliff blame for the uproar at the Grange when he tells Nelly that she should be told to shun him?
tasks.required_document_text: Tell Isabella to shun me; this uproar is owing to her; and should she or any one else aggravate my anger at present, I shall get wild.

tasks.question: How long after her departure did Isabella send her brother a note announcing her marriage with Heathcliff?
tasks.required_document_text: I should mention that Isabella sent to her brother, some six weeks from her departure, a short note, announcing her marriage with Heathcliff.

tasks.question: How many times does Nelly say she flatly refused Heathcliff before he forced her to an agreement?
tasks.required_document_text: Lockwood, I argued and complained, and flatly refused him fifty times; but in the long run he forced me to an agreement.

tasks.question: How long after his sister's death did Hindley Earnshaw's own end follow?
tasks.required_document_text: The end of Earnshaw was what might have been expected; it followed fast on his sister’s: there were scarcely six months between them.

tasks.question: Until what age of Miss Cathy did time wear on at the Grange in its former pleasant way?
tasks.required_document_text: Time wore on at the Grange in its former pleasant way till Miss Cathy reached sixteen.

tasks.question: At what hour did Nelly set out on foot hoping to creep into Wuthering Heights and up to Linton's room unobserved?
tasks.required_document_text: I went at five o’clock, and walked; fancying I might manage to creep into the house, and up to Linton’s room, unobserved.

tasks.question: At what hour did Heathcliff come and inquire whether Miss Linton had risen?
tasks.required_document_text: At seven o’clock he came, and inquired if Miss Linton had risen.

tasks.question: How long before Lockwood's arrival did Nelly have her long talk with Zillah on the moor?
tasks.required_document_text: I had a long talk with Zillah about six weeks ago, a little before you came, one day when we foregathered on the moor; and this is what she told me.

tasks.question: For how long had Lockwood agreed to rent Thrushcross Grange, and where was he setting out for next week?
tasks.required_document_text: I shall set out for London next week; and I must give you warning that I feel no disposition to retain Thrushcross Grange beyond the twelve months I agreed to rent it.

tasks.question: Who made up the whole attendance at Heathcliff's burial, according to Nelly?
tasks.required_document_text: Earnshaw and I, the sexton, and six men to carry the coffin, comprehended the whole attendance.
